Location: Lake Okeechobee north shore – S-135 (J&S Fish Camp, Martin Co.), G-36 (Henry Creek), S-127 (Buckhead Ridge), S-131 (Lakeport)
Item: Four north-shore Lake Okeechobee boat locks still closed around the clock
Details: South Florida Water Management District's Oct 12 navigation notice lists S-135, G-36, S-127 and S-131 as closed 24 hours a day, 7 days a week; the District says it plans to reopen them "in the coming weeks." Lake Okeechobee has been low since summer. Why it matters: these locks are the side doors between the lake and the north-shore canals and fish camps – if you were planning to tuck into Buckhead Ridge or Lakeport, you can't get there from the lake right now. The main Okeechobee Waterway (Port Mayaca, Moore Haven, Ortona, St. Lucie, Franklin) is a separate set of Corps locks and isn't covered by this notice.
When: Since July 2026 (low water); notice Oct 12 2026 – reopening 'in the coming weeks', no date
Notes: What to do: call the lock operator, Advanced Lock Tender Division, at 863-532-8042 before heading for any north-shore lock; SFWMD general line 561-686-8800 (800-432-2045 in Florida). Use S-193 at Taylor Creek (open daily again – see Route Open row) to reach Okeechobee town. Also remember the Point Chosen swing bridge on Route 2 is limited to 8 ft clearance through Dec 22 (already in the sheet) – sailboats crossing the lake should plan on Route 1 (open lake) and check depths with lake levels this low. SFWMD's page gives no reason for the closures; low water is from WGCU's Sept 25 report. No map point – four separate locks.

Location: S-193 Taylor Creek boat lock, Okeechobee (north shore of Lake Okeechobee)
Item: Taylor Creek lock (S-193) back to daily operation
Details: S-193 at Taylor Creek, which had been open weekends only since late September after a summer low-water closure, is now listed as open seven days a week, 5:30am–9pm, in the South Florida Water Management District's Oct 12 notice. Why it matters: it's the boater's gateway from the lake into the town of Okeechobee – fuel, groceries and restaurants – and you no longer have to time a weekday crossing around a closed lock.
Notes: What to do: arrive before 9pm; lock operator (Advanced Lock Tender Division) 863-532-8042. The other four north-shore locks are still closed (see ICW Alert row). The SFWMD notice doesn't say exactly which day daily hours resumed – Start Date is the notice date. Map point: Okeechobee town center (approximate; the lock is on Taylor Creek just southeast of town).

Location: Galveston to Port Aransas (Gulf of Mexico, offshore along the Texas coast)
Item: 39th Harvest Moon Regatta – the offshore race to Port Aransas
Details: Lakewood Yacht Club's 39th annual Harvest Moon Regatta, sponsored by the Bay Access Sailing Foundation, starts Thursday Oct 22 at 2pm; awards are Saturday Oct 24 at 7pm in Port Aransas, with trophies for both racing and cruising classes. Why it matters: it's one of the Gulf's signature offshore races – cruisers and racers sail through the night under the October moon – and if you're moving down the Texas coast this week you'll share the water with a fleet headed the same way.
When: Start Thu Oct 22 2026, 2pm; awards Sat Oct 24, 7pm
Notes: What to do: if you're making the Galveston–Port Aransas run Oct 22–24, expect a big fleet offshore and keep a sharp watch at night; Port Aransas marinas will be busy that weekend – call ahead for a slip. Contacts are on harvestmoonregatta.com/hmr-contacts. Uncertainty: the 2026 page doesn't give the start line or distance; past years started off the Pleasure Pier in Galveston and ran about 150 nautical miles – check the 2026 race documents. Map point: Port Aransas (finish).

Location: Lake Pontchartrain, New Orleans – New Orleans YC, Pontchartrain YC, Southern YC, Tammany YC
Details: The Gulf Yachting Association schedule lists the Lake Pontchartrain Racing Circuit for Oct 23–25, hosted jointly by New Orleans Yacht Club, Pontchartrain Yacht Club, Southern Yacht Club and Tammany Yacht Club. Why it matters: it's the four lake clubs' shared fall regatta – a weekend when Lake Pontchartrain fills with racing sailboats, good watching from the lakefront.
Notes: What to do: give race areas room if you're crossing the lake that weekend; check the host clubs' sites for the notice of race and course areas. Uncertainty: only the dates and hosts are confirmed for 2026 (GYA schedule); format, start and finish venues weren't found – earlier listings say the circuit was started in 1985 by the four clubs, not confirmed on a 2026 page. Same weekend as Mobile YC's Charity Regatta (Oct 23–25) and Bay-Waveland YC's Monk Smith and Gulf Coast Melges 15 Championship (Oct 24–25) on the GYA schedule. No map point – four host clubs.

Location: John's Pass Village & Boardwalk, 12850 Village Blvd, Madeira Beach
Details: Madeira Beach's three-day seafood festival on the John's Pass boardwalk, hosted by the Madeira Beach Recreation Department. Why it matters: John's Pass is right on the Gulf ICW between Treasure Island and Madeira Beach – a festival you can practically tie up to, but expect heavy boat and bridge traffic at the pass all weekend.
Notes: What to do: if transiting John's Pass that weekend, go slow and expect crowded docks; call area marinas ahead for a slip. Parking ashore is $4/hr in city lots, with a free Jolley Trolley shuttle from City Hall. The '45th annual' and daily hours come from secondary listings; the organizer page gives only the overall noon Friday – 6pm Sunday window. Same weekend as DIYC's Halloween Regatta in Tampa (Oct 24, in the sheet).
